exceptions.reason: three.js ships pre-bundled single-module artifacts (three.module / three.core / three.webgpu). Chunking is module-granular — a single module cannot be divided. All three chunks are lazy: they load only for playground/scene routes, and the WebGPU widget layer is disabled by default (AGENTS.md rule 18).

virtual:i18n-boot/<locale>/<section> generates one atomic payload module per locale section — each i18n-<locale>-<section> chunk IS the fetch unit, equivalent to one translations JSON. Only the active locale's section is ever requested; other locales lazy-load on language switch.

virtual:docs-manifest emits the full docs tree as one atomic generated module, lazy-loaded only on the /docs route. Splitting requires restructuring the docs-portal manifest generator — tracked as a follow-up.
@firebase packages ship as pre-bundled dist modules — module-granular splitting cannot divide them. Loaded only by the CMS entry, never on the public site's critical path (the site uses REST).

onnxruntime-web ships as one pre-bundled artifact (ort.webgpu.bundle.min) — module-granular splitting cannot divide it. Strictly lazy: reachable only through ort-engine's dynamic import(), fires on first ML inference call, and the whole layer degrades to null when unavailable. Absent from legacy tiers entirely (ort-legacy-stub plugin in vite.config.js).
